newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: U.N. official says Cambodia fears "assuaged".
newsitem.headline: U.N. official says Cambodia fears "assuaged".

text.p: A top U.N. official flew out of Cambodia on Saturday saying his concerns about the political situation had been partly allayed after meeting the country's two feuding premiers during a brief visit.

"I raised some of the concerns that were felt by the Secretary General (Kofi Annan) as well as some of the U.N. member states about the apparent deterioration in the situation in Cambodia," Alvaro de Soto said of his separate meetings on Friday with co-premiers Prince Norodom Ranariddh and Hun Sen.

"To some extent the concerns were assuaged," he said, in reference to the increasingly tense relations between the two men and their parties since a deadly March 30 grenade attack on an opposition rally killed up to 19 people.
De Soto, assistant secretary general for political affairs, said that after meeting the two premiers he believed they could still work together.
"I think it's possible and obviously this is something the international community looks at them to do," he said.

But he said that until the culprit or culprits behind the March 30 grenade attack were brought to justice, "There is a danger that incidents of this type might be repeated and this could have a dampening effect on the general stability of the country but also on the electoral process."

"It is obviously in everyone's interests that this matter be investigated properly," he said of the protest led by Sam Rainsy, an ally of Ranariddh and his royalist FUNCINPEC party and bitter foe of Hun Sen and his Cambodian People's Party (CPP).
FUNCINPEC and the CPP formed an uneasy coalition government after U.N.-run elections in 1993 and are expected to battle each other in local and general elections due by the end of 1998.

De Soto said he had also discussed the future U.N. role in Cambodia, including maintenance of the office of the U.N. secretary general's special representative, and U.N. assistance in coordinating international assistance for the elections.
He said the current special representative, Benny Widyono of Indonesia, would be replaced "very soon".
